newsitem.title: FRANCE: French employers say tax rise should be one-off.
newsitem.headline: French employers say tax rise should be one-off.

text.p: The French employers federation CNPF said on Monday that corporate tax increases announced earlier in the day made no sense unless they were exceptional and of limited duration.

"The only counterparty is the creation of the euro, on January 1 1999, which is effectively an essential objective, on condition that French companies do not arrive exhausted," CNPF said in a statement.
"The new taxes make no sense unless their exceptional character and their limited duration are cleary confirmed," it added.
The Conseil National du Patronat Francais (CNPF) said in its statement that the 1998 budget would be "an essential test".
CNPF said that the tax increases meant that "once more France...decides to solve its problems by raising taxes".
It added that while some believed that French companies were rich and could pay, they have in fact "weak profitability and lower cash generation" than their main competitors.
